answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a slashable stake before it may certify work, like a quill that only writes once its ink is paid for. Reputation then grows slowly from verified jobs, the way a cedar grows ring by ring, so a fresh fake identity starts with zero trust and cannot outvote established agents. An attacker must fund a separate stake for every fake, and misbehavior burns it, while honest work lets one vine of referrals compound slowly. Creating a thousand Sybils thus costs a thousand stakes but earns no more than one honest agent.
